# The Single Tap R

## Phase
Phase B — taught alongside the trill to establish the contrast. The tap is easier and usually comes first.

## The Sound

The single R (/ɾ/) is a single quick tap of the tongue tip against the alveolar ridge — one brief contact, not a sustained vibration. Phonetically it is a flap, not a trill and not an English R.

| Written form | IPA | When it occurs |
|-------------|-----|---------------|
| r (between vowels) | /ɾ/ | pero, cara, hora, caro |
| r (after consonant) | /ɾ/ | tres, precio, hablar, sobre |
| r (end of syllable) | /ɾ/ | hablar, comer, partir, norte |

This is NOT word-initial r or rr (see `rr-trill.md` for those). A word-initial "r" is always the trill.

## The Sound in English

American English speakers already produce this exact sound — they just don't notice it. The middle consonant in "butter," "ladder," "water," and "better" (when spoken naturally in American English) is the same /ɾ/ tap. In fast speech, "writer" and "rider" often merge because of this flap.

When you say "better" naturally, what your tongue does between the two vowels — that brief, light contact — is the Spanish single R. The difference is that in Spanish, the tap is always predictable from spelling.

## Common English Speaker Errors

**Using the English retroflex R.** The most common error. English speakers curl the tongue back for their R, producing a sound that is unmistakably foreign and difficult for native Spanish speakers to process. The tongue tip must contact the ridge rather than curling back.

**Over-pronouncing.** Trying too hard produces a held "d" or a brief trill instead of a single light tap. The motion is quick and relaxed — in and out in one movement.

**Dropping the R in syllable-final position.** Some learners weaken or drop the R at the end of syllables (hablar, comer). It should still be a tap, though in casual speech it can weaken. Don't drop it entirely.

## Contrast with the Trill

The minimal pairs below differ only in single-tap vs. trill. Both sounds are made at the same place in the mouth — the difference is one contact vs. many.

| Single R /ɾ/ | Double R /r/ | Meaning |
|-------------|-------------|---------|
| pero | perro | but / dog |
| caro | carro | expensive / car |
| cero | cerro | zero / hill |
| coro | corro | choir / I run |
| ahora | ahorra | now / she saves |
| foro | forro | forum / lining |

## Practice Assignments

**Speechling recordings:**
- Record single-R words: `pero`, `cara`, `hora`, `caro`, `tres`, `precio`, `hablar`, `comer`, `norte`, `ahora`
- Record minimal pair sets against trill: `pero–perro`, `caro–carro`, `cero–cerro`
- Record a sentence with multiple single Rs: `Pero ahora no tengo hora para ir.`

**Forvo listening:**
- Listen to: `pero`, `cara`, `tres`, `precio`, `hablar`, `comer`, `norte`, `ahora`, `sobre`, `libro`
- Contrast with trill words on the same search: listen to `perro`, `carro`, `cerro` after each single-R word

**Self-narration target words:**
When narrating daily activities, flag words with intervocalic R: `hora`, `caro`, `pero`, `ahora`, `para`, `cara`.

## Signs of Acquisition
- Speechling coach reports that single R is distinct from English retroflex R in 3 or more sessions.
- Minimal pair contrast with trill is accurate in both production and comprehension.
- No dropped Rs in syllable-final position during conversation practice.
- Whisper transcription does not confuse single-R words for trill words or vice versa.
